idiom_name: Azure Service Bus ServiceBusSender + ServiceBusProcessor with async handlers
implementation_notes: The .NET SDK ships the endpoint construct: ServiceBusSender.SendMessageAsync covers the outbound direction, while ServiceBusProcessor is an event-based abstraction over a set of receivers whose ProcessMessageAsync/ProcessErrorAsync delegates the adapter assigns before calling StartProcessingAsync - so the application-facing adapter stays thin and can be registered as a singleton service. Map ServiceBusReceivedMessage to application calls and application data to ServiceBusMessage inside the adapter, keeping Azure types out of the application; MassTransit or NServiceBus consumers play the same role on other transports. The same shape works with any client whose API exposes a processor/receiver (ServiceBusReceiver.ReceiveMessagesAsync for the polling variant).
pitfalls: AutoCompleteMessages defaults to true with PeekLock: if the handler throws, the message must be abandoned or dead-lettered explicitly, otherwise a fire-and-forget handler turns into silent message loss.
A processor must be started explicitly and disposed asynchronously - abandoned processors leak AMQP links and keep the client connection alive.
ProcessMessageAsync runs concurrently up to MaxConcurrentCalls, so per-message state belongs in the handler arguments, never on the adapter instance.
